Turn the fractions of box answers into pixel positions

Source: R/decide_media.R
box_to_pixels.Rd

A box answer from field_box() gives top, bottom, left and right as fractions of the image. box_to_pixels() multiplies them by the image size, after clamping them to 0 and 1, and returns your decide() result with four more columns: x_min, x_max, y_min and y_max, in pixels counted from the top-left corner. Rows that are not boxes, or whose type is missing, get NA. The pixel values are rounded to whole pixels. If .result already has pixel columns from an earlier call, they are replaced.

Usage

box_to_pixels(.result, .width = NULL, .height = NULL, .image = NULL)

Arguments

.result

A decide() result that holds a field_box() question.

.width, .height

Image width and height in pixels, one number each.

.image

Instead of .width and .height, the path of the PNG or JPEG file the boxes refer to; its size is read from the file. If you give it, .width and .height are ignored.

Value

.result with the columns x_min, x_max, y_min and y_max.

Details

Clamping keeps each edge inside the image but does not repair a box the model returned upside down: if left is larger than right, x_min stays larger than x_max. Widths and heights need not be whole numbers.

The result must come from one image size. If your states are images of different sizes, filter the result by state_id and call the function once per size.

See also

field_box()

Examples

res <- tibble::tibble(question = "cat", type = "box",
                      top = 0.2, bottom = 0.7, left = 0, right = 0.8)
box_to_pixels(res, .width = 1000, .height = 600)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 10
#>   question type    top bottom  left right x_min x_max y_min y_max
#>   <chr>    <chr> <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 cat      box     0.2    0.7     0   0.8     0   800   120   420
